title.narrative: Timor Leste Road Climate Resilience Project

description.narrative: The objective of the Road Climate Resilience Project for Timor Leste is to deliver climate resilient road infrastructure to the beneficiary communities on key road links and facilitate emergency responses to tackle natural disasters. There are three components to the project. The first component of the project is climate resilient road infrastructure. This component will invest in the key road infrastructure on the Dili-Ainaro corridor to improve the corridor's climate resilience. The second component of the project is climate responsive maintenance and emergency planning and response systems. The third component of the project is project support and training. This component includes: 1) support to the Project Management Unit (PMU); 2) training program for government staff and contractors as necessary; and, 3) independent safeguards monitoring.
The project will deliver sustainable climate resilient road infrastructure on the Dili-Ainaro corridor.

title.narrative: Number of locations with improved slope protection on the Dili-Ainaro corridor

comment.narrative:
<p>?????Number of locations with improved slope protection: Lot 1 – 112, Lot 2 – <strong>493</strong>, Lot 3 – 235, Lot 4 – 244, and Lot 5 – 266.</p>

<p>Stone masonry retaining wall: 352 out of 362 Locations.</p>

<p>Gabion: 141 out of 141 locations.</p>

title.narrative: Improvement in road condition in the Dili-Ainaro corridor measured by reduced road roughness

comment.narrative: <p>Final IRI of 3.43 m/km results from the average IRI of 2.94 m/km for Lot 1 (10.0km), 3.83 m/km for Lot 2 (22.6 km), and 3.29 m/km for Lot 3 (29.4 km).</p>

target.value: 85% of the road under Defects Liability Period / PBM is compliant with the contractual service level on an annual basis.

comment.narrative:
<p>Lot. 2 Project was <strong>93.94%</strong> as per Variation Order No. 2.</p>

<p>However, the project was taken over as per As-built (Variation Order No. 3) which the achievement actual completion was <strong>$16,542,026.34 <strong>(</strong></strong97.28%).</p>

<p>???????The length of paved road was 22.21km.</p>

<p>Remaining work due to Force majeure Events is <strong>$462,737.61</strong> (2.72%).</p>

actual.value: The two-year PBM ended in July 2019 for Lot 1, June 2021 for Lot 3, November 2021 for Lot 4, and February 2022 for Lot 5. For Lot 2, the four-year PBM will start in June 2024.

title.narrative: Roads in good and fair condition as a share of total classified roads

comment.narrative: <p>As of December 31, 2022, the progress was as follows: Lot 1 (10 km) 100%; Lot 2 (22.62 km) 98.19%; Lot 3 (29.47 km), 100%; Lot 4 (24.75 km) 100%; Lot 5 (22.65 km) 100%.</p>

title.narrative: Increase in drainage in good condition on the Dili-Ainaro corridor

comment.narrative:
<p>110% of Achievement. </p>
<p>As of December 31, 2022, the progress achieved was as follows: Lot 1 (10 km) 100%; Lot 2 (22.62 km), 99.81%; Lot 3 (29.47 km) 100%; Lot 4 (24.75 km) 100%; and Lot 5 (22.65 km) 100%.</p>

title.narrative: Increase in average daily traffic (ADT) measured by total vehicles per day on the Dili-Ainaro corridor

comment.narrative: <p>Compared to the 2014 ADT of 835 vehicles per day, the 2023 ADT of 2,926 vehicles per day was 250 percent increase. </p>

title.narrative: Reduction in the number of incidents requiring emergency repairs on the Dili-Ainaro corridor

comment.narrative: <p>The unit of measure changed from percentage to number of incidents, and the target was achieved, given the value at closure was three: a tree felt down to a house in April 2022, a fatal incident in August 2022, and a second fatal incident in September 2022.</p>

title.narrative: Grievances registered related to delivery of project benefits addressed

comment.narrative: <p>By 22 November 2022 there were 53 grievances reported, from which 4 grievances related to environmental, health & safety issue, 43 social issues and 6 issues of resettlement. All issues were in Lot 2 project.</p>

title.narrative: Grievances responded and/or resolved within the stipulated service standards for response times

comment.narrative:
<p>By 22 November 2022 there were 53 grievances reported, from which 4 grievances related to environmental, health & safety issue, 43 social issues and 6 issues of resettlement. All issues were in Lot 2 project.</p>

<p>All grievances were solved on time and only 1 issue solved after 3 months. In November and December 2022, no grievances were reported. </p>
